units.title: Holidays
units.intro: Grammar and writing: composition writing and basic paragraphing (topic sentence, supporting sentences, concluding sentence).

cards.title: Basic paragraph structure
rule: A **paragraph** develops **one main idea**. It has: (1) a **topic sentence** that states the idea; (2) **supporting sentences** with reasons, facts and examples; (3) a **concluding sentence** that sums up or links to the next paragraph.
A **composition** has an **introduction** (topic and main point), **body paragraphs** (one idea each) and a **conclusion**.

examples.text: Topic sentence: Holidays help families grow closer.
A paragraph that jumps from holidays to football to exams.
examples.fix: Keep one main idea per paragraph.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.

steps.text: The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]').
This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.

steps.text: The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership.
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has').

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The candidate ________ the board selected for the position has outstanding credentials.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The relative pronoun refers to 'The candidate' (a person). The clause that follows has a subject-verb pattern: 'the board' (Subject) + 'selected' (Verb). This indicates the relative pronoun is acting as the object of 'selected'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
While 'who' is increasingly used as an object pronoun in casual speech, formal academic exams strictly enforce 'whom' for objective relative slots ($$\text{Whom} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ን 'The candidate' (ሰብ) ክውክል ከሎ፡ ድሕሪኡ ዘሎ ሓረግ 'the board selected' (Subject + Verb) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ኣብ ቦታ ተቐባሊ (object) እዩ ዘሎ። ስለዚ ኣብ ስሩዕ ሰዋስው 'whom' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'Who' ኣብ ናይ ዋና ባእታ (subject) ቦታ ጥራይ እዩ ዝስራዕ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Since both Almaz and her sister wanted to complete the project quickly, they did all the research ________.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The subject is 'they' (plural). The corresponding plural reflexive pronoun is 'themselves' ($$\text{They} \rightarrow \text{themselves}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Options A ('theirselves') and D ('by theirselves') are non-standard forms. Tigrinya speakers often use 'theirselves' because they translate 'ባዕላቶም' directly based on the possessive modifier 'their'.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ናይ 'they' (ንሳቶም) ነብሰ-ኣንጸባራቒ ተውላጠ ስም (reflexive pronoun) 'themselves' (Option B - ባዕላቶም) እዩ። 'Theirselves' ዝብል ቃል ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ሰዋስው ፈጺሙ የለን፤ እዚ ልሙድ ናይ ተማሃሮ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Unity and coherence
rule: **Unity:** every sentence supports the topic sentence; remove sentences that do not. **Coherence:** ideas follow a clear order and are joined with linkers: *first, then, after that, finally; for example, in addition, however; in conclusion*.

examples.text: First we packed. Then we travelled to Massawa. Finally we rested.
In conclusion is used at the start of the first paragraph.
examples.fix: In conclusion belongs in the last paragraph.

cards.pattern: Topic sentence → support (reasons + examples) → concluding sentence

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "In conclusion is used at the start of the first paragraph."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **Unity:** every sentence supports the topic sentence; remove sentences that do not. **Coherence:** ideas follow a clear order and are joined with linkers: *first, then, after that, finally; for example, in addition, however; in conclusion*.
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "In conclusion is used at the start of the first paragraph." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "In conclusion belongs in the last paragraph."

cards.answer: In conclusion belongs in the last paragraph.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **T-S-C**: Tell (topic sentence), Support (reasons and examples), Close (concluding sentence).

cards.title: Unit summary
body: A paragraph has one main idea: topic sentence, supporting sentences and a concluding sentence. A composition has an introduction, body paragraphs and a conclusion. Good writing has unity (everything on topic) and coherence (clear order and linkers).

glossary.meaning: The sentence that states the main idea of a paragraph.
All sentences support one main idea.
